rubricRules.ruleName: Runtime Efficiency and Data Access Patterns
rubricRules.ruleDescription:
<scanner_behavior> DEDUP = Same issue in one file produces ONE finding listing all locations. No duplicates. SEVERITY = Locked to the claim. A HIGH claim always produces a HIGH finding. RECOMMENDATIONS = Concrete, copy-pasteable edits only. PROHIBITED -- "verify", "consider", "review whether", "ensure that", "check if". For IaC/SDK/architecture fixes, copy-pasteable means structural pseudocode or a doc-pointer to the authoritative AWS/SDK docs, NOT a generated CDK/CloudFormation/Terraform/SDK code block. CONFIDENCE = HIGH findings require confidence certain. If uncertain, downgrade to an observation. GROUNDING = Report only what you directly observed via tools or file reading. No inference. ANTI-PATTERNS = Do NOT flag code labeled BAD EXAMPLE / anti-pattern / "Don't do this". That content is teaching, not violating. SECURITY EXCLUSION = Runs AFTER a Content Security Review. Do NOT flag security (secrets, IAM scope, encryption, network exposure, app-sec). Evaluate ONLY code quality and documentation. NO EXECUTION = Holmes does not run code or profile; judge static textual evidence only. </scanner_behavior>
Avoids structural performance anti-patterns that would degrade at scale. Non-blocking (worst case MEDIUM).
<calibration> DEFENSIBLE-ALTERNATIVE = Do NOT flag code that is a reasonable choice with a plausible rationale, even if a faster form exists; flag only a violated_by match or a structural anti-pattern that demonstrably degrades at scale. OPINION-IS-A-NOTE = A micro-optimization preference with no violated_by match -> record as a note (does not fail the rule), not a finding. MATURITY = Near-production bar: flag structural anti-patterns that degrade at realistic customer data volumes; do not flag micro-optimizations on genuinely bounded, small data. DO / DON'T = DO flag an N+1 call in a hot path where a batch API exists, or an unbounded scan/list on growing data; DON'T flag a loop over a known-small bounded collection, or constant kwargs in a loop. </calibration>
<scope> IN SCOPE: N+1 service/DB calls inside loops where batch APIs exist; O(N^2) nested iteration where a map/set lookup is straightforward; unconsumed pagination (NextToken/markers); unbounded list/scan without limits; loop-invariant recomputation that should be hoisted. OUT OF SCOPE: sync-vs-async design and AWS service selection (-> Architecture Appropriateness topic); module decomposition and duplication (-> Code Structure topic); cold-start latency (platform concern); IaC templates/config (-> Infrastructure-as-Code Quality topic); test files. </scope>
<file_scope> INCLUDE: *.py, *.ts, *.js EXCLUDE: *.md, *.json, *.yaml, *.yml, *.tf, *.sh, *.drawio, *.svg, *.png </file_scope>
<tool_instructions> STEP 1: count_pattern (?im)\b(for|while)\b.{0,400}?\.(get_item|getItem|put_item|putItem|query|scan|get_object|getObject|put_object|putObject|delete_object|deleteObject|send_message|sendMessage|publish|invoke)\s*\( -> same-line AWS/DB calls in loops. this counter is line-based, so it MISSES the common multi-line N+1 (loop header on one line, per-item call below); ALSO read each loop body for per-item service/DB calls. STEP 2: count_pattern (?i)(next_token|nexttoken|continuation_token|continuationtoken|next_marker|nextmarker|last_evaluated_key|lastevaluatedkey|is_truncated|istruncated|paginate|get_paginator) -> presence of pagination handling; absence near a list/scan/query is a candidate unconsumed-pagination signal. STEP 3: Read the code for nested loops over comparably-sized unbounded collections (candidate O(N^2)). Judge by indentation/structure -- this counter is line-based and cannot detect cross-line nesting, so do NOT rely on it here. STEP 4: Judge whether flagged loops operate on unbounded collections and whether a batch API or a map/set lookup is a straightforward alternative. Use counts as evidence, not the sole basis. </tool_instructions>
<claims> <claim id="RE1" severity="HIGH"> No N+1 data access -- individual service/DB calls inside loops where a batch/query API exists. <violated_by> - GetItem/getObject/SendMessage/etc. called once per item inside a loop over an unbounded collection when BatchGetItem/query/SendMessageBatch is available </violated_by> <not_violated_by> - Iteration over a genuinely small, bounded set (e.g., 3-5 AWS regions or a fixed config list) - A single-item per-request operation (one GetItem per event in a per-event handler) - Prototype-scale code with a comment acknowledging batch optimization is needed for production - Framework-imposed ORM lazy-loading the developer cannot override without abandoning the framework </not_violated_by> NOTE: Relocating per-item calls into a service layer or helper does NOT resolve an N+1 -- the loop and its calls move together, so RE1 still fires. Restructuring into a service layer is a Code Structure concern, not a fix for this claim; the batch API must still be applied. FIX: replace per-item calls with the named service batch equivalent (e.g. DynamoDB BatchGetItem, SQS SendMessageBatch); consult SDK docs for exact call shape. </claim>
<claim id="RE2" severity="HIGH"> No O(N^2) nested iteration where a map/set lookup is straightforward. <violated_by> - Nested loops over the same or comparably-sized unbounded collections to find matches where a dict/set index gives O(1) lookup </violated_by> <not_violated_by> - Nested iteration over clearly bounded small sets (2-3 items); algorithms with no straightforward map/set alternative; bounded and documented recursion </not_violated_by> </claim>
<claim id="RE3" severity="HIGH"> Paginated API responses are fully consumed. <violated_by> - List/scan/query calls that process only the first page and ignore NextToken/markers/LastEvaluatedKey, silently dropping remaining data </violated_by> <not_violated_by> - Code that loops on continuation tokens until exhausted, or uses a paginator; a single-page call against a known-small, bounded collection - If no pagination is attempted at all, flag as RE4 instead </not_violated_by> </claim>
<claim id="RE4" severity="HIGH"> Unbounded list/scan operations include pagination or an explicit result limit. <violated_by> - Full table scans or list operations with no limit and no pagination on paths that encounter growing data volumes - If code fetches the first page but ignores NextToken, flag as RE3 instead (do not double-count) </violated_by> <not_violated_by> - Operations with an explicit limit/max-results; queries constrained to a bounded key range; one-time bounded setup data </not_violated_by> </claim>
<claim id="RE5" severity="HIGH"> Loop-invariant expensive computations are hoisted outside the loop. <violated_by> - Re-querying a database or recomputing the same invariant reference data on every loop iteration </violated_by> <not_violated_by> - Computation that genuinely depends on the loop variable; negligible-cost in-loop expressions - Function/method keyword arguments that are string literals or constant/module-level references (e.g. modelId=MODEL, contentType='application/json', max_tokens=8192) -- passing a constant as a kwarg is not recomputation; only flag genuinely expensive invariant work (DB/network queries, large object-graph construction) that is separable from the per-iteration varying inputs </not_violated_by> </claim> </claims>
<choice_formula> exemplary: 0 findings | needs_revision: >=1 finding of any severity | not_applicable: No application source code with runtime logic in scope (config/IaC/docs-only batch) </choice_formula>
